formulations.label: Tablets
formulations.strengths: 15 mg (UK). The clinic's 25 mg tablet has no UK SmPC; UK 15 mg tablet SmPCs used.
formulations.note: No UK product information exists for the 25 mg strength: only 15 mg tablets are licensed in the UK. Doses below are in 15 mg tablets as the UK SmPCs state; convert carefully for a 25 mg tablet. One UK SmPC (the brand) is licensed for motion sickness only; two generic UK SmPCs also cover vestibular disorders.

src.q: Cinnarizine 15 mg Excipients with known effect: lactose monohydrate and sucrose
Each tablet contains 15 mg of cinnarizine.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Generic UK SmPCs: disorders of balance (maintenance therapy for labyrinthine symptoms including vertigo, tinnitus, nystagmus, nausea and vomiting, e.g. Ménière's disease) and motion sickness. The brand UK SmPC: motion sickness only.

src.q: Disorders of balance - maintenance therapy for symptoms of labyrinthine disorders, including vertigo, tinnitus, nystagmus, nausea and vomiting such as is seen in Meniere's Disease.
Cinnarizine is also effective in the control of motion sickness.
Stugeron is effective in the control of motion sickness.

items.t: UK products are 15 mg tablets only; the 25 mg strength is not licensed in the UK. The stated doses should not be exceeded.

src.q: The stated doses should not be exceeded.

items.t: Two 15 mg tablets three times a day (generic UK SmPCs). Do not exceed the stated dose.
items.tag: Vestibular symptoms, adults, elderly and over 12 years

src.q: Vestibular symptoms: Adults, elderly and children over 12 years: Two tablets three times a day.
The stated doses should not be exceeded.

items.t: Two 15 mg tablets 2 hours before travel, then one tablet every 8 hours during the journey.
items.tag: Motion sickness, adults, elderly and over 12 years

src.q: Adults, elderly and children over 12 years: 2 tablets 2 hours before you travel and 1 tablet every 8 hours during your journey.

items.t: Children 5 to 12 years: half the adult dose (vestibular symptoms: one 15 mg tablet three times a day in one generic SmPC). No dose given under 5 years.

src.q: Children 5 to 12 years: One half the adult dose.
Children 5-12 years: One tablet three times a day.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to cinnarizine or any excipient.

src.q: Stugeron should not be given to patients with known hypersensitivity to cinnarizine or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

items.t: Porphyria: contraindicated in one UK SmPC (4.3); the other two UK SmPCs say use should be avoided (4.4).

src.q: Contra-indicated in porphyria and in patients with known hypersensitivity to cinnarizine.
Use of cinnarizine should be avoided in porphyria.

items.t: Parkinson's disease: give only if the advantages outweigh the risk of worsening it.

src.q: In patients with Parkinson's disease, Stugeron should only be given if the advantages outweigh the possible risk of aggravating this disease.

items.t: Hepatic or renal insufficiency: use with care (not studied).

src.q: There have been no specific studies in hepatic or renal dysfunction. Stugeron should be used with care in patients with hepatic or renal insufficiency.

items.t: Somnolence, especially at the start: caution with alcohol, CNS depressants or tricyclic antidepressants. May cause epigastric discomfort (take after meals).

src.q: Stugeron may cause somnolence, especially at the start of treatment.
caution should be taken when alcohol, central nervous system (CNS) depressants or tricyclic antidepressants are used concomitantly
As with other antihistamines, Stugeron may cause epigastric discomfort; taking it after meals may diminish gastric irritation.

items.t: Excipients: contains lactose (and sucrose in the brand product). Patients with hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose or galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase- isomaltase insufficiency, should not take this medicine because it contains lactose and sucrose.

items.t: Skin allergy tests: may suppress a positive reaction if taken within 4 days before testing.

src.q: Stugeron may prevent an otherwise positive reaction to dermal reactivity indicators if used within 4 days prior to testing.

items.t: Alcohol, CNS depressants and tricyclic antidepressants: may potentiate sedation of either drug; use with caution.

src.q: Concurrent use of alcohol, CNS depressants or tricyclic antidepressants may potentiate the sedative effects of either of these drugs or of Stugeron.
caution should be taken when alcohol, central nervous system (CNS) depressants or tricyclic antidepressants are used concomitantly

items.t: Skin testing: may prevent positive reactions if used up to 4 days before.

src.q: Stugeron may prevent otherwise positive reactions to dermal reactivity indicators if used up to 4 days prior to skin testing.

items.t: Not studied; use with care in renal insufficiency. No numeric threshold given.

src.q: Stugeron should be used with care in patients with hepatic or renal insufficiency.

items.t: Not studied; use with care in hepatic insufficiency.

src.q: Stugeron should be used with care in patients with hepatic or renal insufficiency.

items.t: Safety in human pregnancy not established (no teratogenicity in animals); not advisable to give in pregnancy.

src.q: As with other drugs it is not advisable to administer Stugeron in pregnancy.

items.t: No data on excretion in breast milk; not recommended in nursing mothers.

src.q: Use of Stugeron is not recommended in nursing mothers.
Taking cinnarizine whilst breast-feeding is not recommended.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception information in the UK cinnarizine 15 mg SmPCs checked (emc brand SmPC; MHRA generic SPCs).

items.t: Most common in trials: somnolence (9.9%), nausea (3.0%), weight increased (1.5%). Also dyspepsia, fatigue, sweating; headache, dry mouth and hypersensitivity reported.

src.q: the most commonly reported (>1% incidence) Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) were: somnolence (9.9), nausea (3.0) and increased weight (1.5)
Cases of hypersensitivity, headache and dry mouth have been reported.

items.t: Extrapyramidal symptoms (dyskinesia, parkinsonism, tremor, muscle rigidity), sometimes with depressive feelings, mainly in elderly on long-term use: stop treatment.

src.q: Rare cases of aggravation or appearance of extrapyramidal symptoms (sometimes associated with depressive feelings) have been described, predominantly in elderly people during prolonged therapy. The treatment should be discontinued in such cases.

items.t: Cholestatic jaundice; lichenoid keratosis/lichen planus; subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

src.q: Very rare cases of lichen planus, lupus-like skin reactions and cholestatic jaundice have been reported.

items.t: Elderly on long-term treatment: watch for extrapyramidal symptoms; stop if they appear.

src.q: The treatment should be discontinued in such cases.
predominantly in elderly people during prolonged therapy

items.t: Take preferably after meals. Tablets may be sucked, chewed or swallowed whole with water (one generic SmPC).

src.q: Stugeron should preferably be taken after meals.
The tablets may be sucked, chewed or swallowed whole with water.

items.t: May cause drowsiness, especially at first: do not drive or use machines if affected. Avoid alcohol.

src.q: Stugeron may cause drowsiness, especially at the start of treatment; patients affected in this way should not drive or operate machinery.
Avoid alcoholic drink.

items.t: Stop 4 days before skin allergy testing.
